dimensions.explanation: The selected control concerns intermediaries distributing SFC-authorised funds and promotion to a client of a specific product or particular product type. Section 103's person issuing an invitation to the Hong Kong public has a distinct scope.

Actual fund return and distributor top-up are distinguished, but gift, discount and economically inseparable combined benefits lack complete classification tests. Guaranteed returns may constitute structured products or gifts; neither classification is automatic.

The fee-or-charge discount exception modifies gifts. A qualifying discount does not itself exempt a distinct gift in the same offer. Authorisation and exemption in section 103 attach separately to that offence description.

The selected rule says should not offer; gift classification says may be considered. These are preserved without converting the selected control into a statutory offence or treating all incentives as gifts. Other passages separately describe an offence, mandatory advertising compliance and possible regulatory action.
2010-09-30 dates the referenced FAQ, not commencement of the selected rule. The circular date, operative Code version and transition provisions are absent. No date condition is inferred.

The text invokes section 103, paragraph 3.11 and a FAQ despite an empty packet dependency list. Their full contents and applicable versions are unavailable. Even where makes the gift issue independently relevant when structured-product status is absent; it does not restrict the gift rule exclusively to that situation. Disclosure and advertising dependencies concern separate controls.

readings.distinction: This reading includes product-type campaigns without a named individual fund and assesses distinct gift components despite a fee discount elsewhere in the offer. It preserves the qualified classification of guaranteed returns and the independent section 103 path. The source supports unresolved classification questions more strongly than a second materially different rule: a named-product-only restriction, a blanket combined-offer exemption, automatic gift classification, or a non-structured-product prerequisite would each discard express wording. The strongest uncertainty concerns gift-versus-discount classification and inseparable benefits.

facts.meaning: Whether at least one actually offered, separately identifiable benefit component is classified as a gift and is not itself a discount of fees or charges. A discount component does not erase a distinct non-discount gift. Guaranteed returns are not automatically gifts. False requires sufficient evidence that no offered component meets both conditions; unresolved classification remains unknown.

readings.statement: [TRUE_IS_PROHIBITED] For the selected paragraph 10 gift control, true means the selected offer is within the distributor, client and product-or-type promotional scope and includes an offered gift component that is not a discount of fees or charges, so it is caught by the quoted should-not-offer restriction. False means at least one necessary condition is established to be absent; it does not establish whole-firm compliance, licence possession or satisfaction of section 103 or other controls. The marker preserves the quoted modality and does not characterize this control as a statutory offence. A guaranteed return or incentive requires classification before the result can be determined.
